Partly fixed in bcacaa03, partly disagreeing.

Fixed: `scanned_child_pids` now streams `/proc` (`proc_pids()`) instead of materializing every pid, and stops one past `CHILD_GROUPS_SCAN_LIMIT` — one past is all the caller needs to return `None`, so the child-group fallback fails closed without reading the rest of the process table. Split out `scanned_child_pids_from` so the bound and the ppid filter are unit tested.

Not changing: the member-discovery sweep in `foreground_process_group_members_with` stays uncapped on purpose. Membership is decided by pgid, and `/proc` has no pgid -> pid index, so finding a group's members is inherently a full sweep — `session_processes()` in this same file already does exactly that for session ids. A cap there would truncate by readdir order, which is where the process this PR is about tends to land (the agent is spawned after its wrapper, so it has the higher pid), and would silently reintroduce the bug on busy hosts. The sweep only runs at all when the kernel probe reports no children files, and only when `should_probe_foreground_job` lets a probe through.

On materializing pids in that path specifically: the cost is the readdir plus one `/proc/<pid>/stat` read per pid, and streaming does not avoid either since every candidate must be inspected anyway. The `Vec` itself is a few thousand `u32`s, and it is the seam that keeps these functions injectable in tests, so I would rather keep it.

@akbash-bot wdyt?

Please inspect this review and reply in this thread.

@ogulcancelik The extra round trip is real, but I think it is the right tradeoff here. The check must happen immediately before each API operation: caching once per CLI process would reopen the exact stale-server gap if an install/handoff replaces the server between `plugin.list` and `plugin.link`. A wait subscription is pinged once before it opens, not once per event, and these are bounded local socket/pipe round trips. I would not weaken or cache this without measured latency showing a problem. If it does become material, the clean optimization is same-connection protocol negotiation/dispatch, not skipping per-operation validation.
